en: The Lord pervades all this—whatever moves in this world.
By renouncing it, you should enjoy; do not covet the wealth of anyone. 1.
Performing actions here in this world, one should desire to live for a hundred years;
thus it is with you, and not otherwise than this—for action does not cling to a person.
"Sunless indeed are those worlds, shrouded in blind darkness;
to them go after death those people who are slayers of the Self. (3)
One, unmoving, swifter than the mind— this, as it sped forth, even the gods could not overtake;
standing still, it outstrips others who run.
In that [fire], Mātariśvan places the waters. || 4 ||
It moves, and it does not move; it is far away, and it is near;
it is within this whole world, and it is outside of this whole world.
But he who perceives all beings in the Self alone,
and the Self in all beings, does not feel aversion toward anything thereafter.
When for the one who perceives all beings have become the Self alone, what delusion and what sorrow can there be for him who beholds this oneness? (7)
He has pervaded all— pure, bodiless, woundless, without sinews, clean, unpierced by evil;
he is the seer, the wise one, the encompasser, the self-existent.
He established the objects of experience according to their true nature for eternal years. || 8 ||
Into blinding darkness enter those who worship ignorance;
into a darkness even greater than that enter those who delight in knowledge alone. 9.
"One thing they say is attained through knowledge, and another thing they say is attained through ignorance;
thus we have heard from the wise who explained this to us. (10)
He who knows both knowledge and ignorance together—having crossed over death by means of ignorance, he enjoys immortality by means of knowledge. 11.
Into blind darkness enter those who worship the Unmanifest; into even greater darkness, as it were, than that, enter those who delight in the Manifest. 12.

"They say that [reality] is one thing from the perspective of manifestation, and they say it is another from the perspective of non-manifestation; thus have we heard from the wise who explained this to us. (13)
He who knows both origin and destruction together—having crossed over death by means of destruction, he enjoys immortality through origin. 14.
The face of truth is covered by a golden vessel;
O Pūṣan, uncover it for me, who am devoted to the law of truth, so that I may see. 15.
O Pūṣan, sole seer, Yama, Sūrya, son of Prajāpati, spread out your rays and gather together your splendor; that form of yours which is most auspicious, that [form] of yours— [behold it].
I see that which I am: that person is indeed myself.
The wind has departed, this body is mortal and ends in ashes. Om! O Kratu, remember; remember what was done; O Kratu, remember; remember what was done. 17.
O Agni, lead us by a good path to wealth, O God who knowest all ways;
keep away from us the sin that leads astray.
We offer you our most abundant words of homage. || 18 ||
Thus ends the Īśopaniṣad.
